headline: Why Tough Cuts Work Best for Braising
snippet: The goal of braising is to transform tough, inexpensive cuts of beef into a tender, succulent dish. The success of this process depends on the selection of meat characterized by a high concentration of connective tissue. When subjected to low, steady heat over several hours, this collagen breaks down into gelatin, which provides a rich mouthfeel and ensures the meat remains moist. Conversely, tender muscles intended for quick searing lack this structural support; when cooked for long periods, they lose their moisture and become dry. Selecting the Cut The most effective cuts for braising are those that worked hardest during the animal's life. The shoulder is a versatile choice, rich in connective tissue and well-suited for classic ragout, goulash, or Boeuf Bourguignon. The neck, with its significant fat marbling and sinew, typically requires 3 to 4 hours of simmering before the meat naturally separates into fibers, making it ideal for pasta sauces and stews. For a more velvet-like consistency in the sauce, the brisket is preferred due to its high fat and collagen content, especially when cooked on the bone. The shank (osso buco) contains a high proportion of bone and cartilage, requiring 4 to 5 hours of cooking, which makes it the primary choice for hearty soups and aspics. Cheeks offer a refined balance of fat and fiber, resulting in an exceptionally tender texture often reserved for restaurant-style preparations. Finally, the flank (brisket/belly) provides a budget-friendly option with fat streaks that work well when ground for sauces like Bolognese.

India’s leading multispeciality hospital chain, Apollo Hospitals, has inaugurated the Apollo Diagnostics National Reference Laboratory and Apollo Clinic in Sector 52, Gurugram, following the opening of Apollo Hospital, Gurugram. Dr. Sangita Reddy, Joint Managing Director of Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited, outlined a vision of bringing quality healthcare closer to families and making prevention and early detection part of routine care. She emphasised timely access to medical expertise, earlier detection and preventive care. The newly inaugurated centre brings primary and specialist consultations together with advanced diagnostics, making these services more accessible to families closer to home. Olympic medallist Saina Nehwal attended the inauguration as the chief guest. The new National Reference Laboratory will serve as a diagnostic partner to Apollo Hospitals in Gurugram. Equipped to conduct more than 3,000 tests, the laboratory will feature advanced robotics and AI-enabled Digi-Smart Track technology to support clinical teams with routine investigations and specialised testing. The laboratory team highlighted the importance of diagnostic excellence, with an emphasis on delivering precise and reliable results in time to inform decisions about patient care. The launch also introduced the Apollo Family Health Card, which brings consultations and preventive health benefits together under one plan to help families keep up with routine care. Highlighting the role of emerging technologies, Dr. Sangita Reddy, Joint Managing Director of Apollo Hospitals Enterprise, said, “As healthcare enters an extraordinary era of transformation, with AI, advanced medical technologies and precision medicine reshaping the possibilities of care, we must ensure that progress never comes at the cost of the human connection. Technology must strengthen the human touch, innovation must improve patient outcomes, and excellence must always be anchored in compassion. This is the balance we must strive for as we build the future of healthcare.”

headline: Ahmed bin Saeed honours participants in ‘Cycle Against Cancer’ initiative
snippet: Dubai: His Highness Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Dubai Health, honoured participants in the ‘Cycle Against Cancer’ initiative in recognition of their efforts to support cancer care programmes at Al Jalila Foundation. His Excellency Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence, attended the ceremony and delivered an address. The ceremony was held during a charity gala dinner at Le Méridien Dubai Hotel & Conference Centre in support of Al Jalila Foundation, which plays a vital role in enabling Dubai Health’s vision to advance health for humanity through the integration of Care, Learning, Discovery and Giving. The event was attended by Her Excellency Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg, Chairperson of the Board of Directors of Al Jalila Foundation and Member of the Board of Directors of Dubai Health; Dr. Amer Al Zarooni, CEO of Al Jalila Foundation; Mustafa Al Hashimi, CEO of Wasl Hospitality and Leisure; Ali Mubarak Al Soori, Chief Procurement and Facilities Officer at Emirates Airline; and Guido De Wilde, Founder of ‘Cycle Against Cancer’, along with several supporters of the initiative. Hosted by presenter Tom Urquhart, the evening featured a charity auction. The initiative raised AED3,333,000, reflecting the 3,333 kilometres covered by participants during the ride. His Highness Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum commended the participants and supporters of ‘Cycle Against Cancer’, saying the initiative embodies the values of giving and solidarity rooted in the UAE community and underscores the importance of joint efforts in service of humanity. His Highness said: “This ride demonstrates how sport can bring people together to make a meaningful difference in the lives of patients and their families, while inspiring hope. We are proud to support initiatives that reflect the values of solidarity and social responsibility and contribute to Dubai Health’s vision to advance health for humanity.” In his address, His Excellency Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan said that His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the UAE, has consistently reminded us that the wellbeing of people must remain at the centre of national development. He said His Highness the President inspires us to recognise that a nation draws strength from its achievements, the compassion of its people and the care it provides to those in need. His Excellency said that His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, places great importance on the wellbeing of the population and has demonstrated an extraordinary commitment to humanitarian service. He added: “Al Jalila Foundation, established by His Highness, exemplifies that commitment. By enabling patients to receive proper treatment, its investment in medical research, and its encouragement of future healthcare professionals, the Foundation brings hope to individuals and families facing enormous challenges. We deeply admire the mission of the Foundation. Thank you to all those whose dedication makes its work possible.” His Excellency said: “One of the great strengths of the United Arab Emirates is that people from many nations, cultures, and traditions have made their lives here. Fifteen cyclists, representing several nationalities, have united in a common humanitarian purpose. Supported by families, friends, colleagues, and corporate partners, they have demonstrated that compassion knows no boundaries of nationality, religion, or culture.” He added that cycling from Barcelona to Paris over 25 days required exceptional determination, discipline and mutual support. “They chose to use their strength and determination in the service of people facing a far greater challenge. For that, they deserve our admiration and heartfelt congratulations.” His Excellency said that “every contribution made this evening has the potential to change a life” and encouraged those in attendance to continue supporting the humanitarian initiative. “The cyclists have completed their journey from Barcelona to Paris. But the journey of compassion and service that they have inspired must continue,” he added. Her Excellency Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg said: “The initiative highlights the important role of the community in advancing charitable and humanitarian efforts. The funds raised will support cancer care programmes at Al Jalila Foundation, as well as scientific research aimed at developing treatments and improving patient outcomes, in line with Dubai Health's 'Patient First' promise.” The journey ‘Cycle Against Cancer’ set off from Barcelona, Spain, on 1 July 2026 and reached Paris, France, after a 25-day journey. The 15 cyclists covered 3,333 kilometres along routes with a cumulative elevation gain of more than 54,000 metres. The ride brought together cancer survivors, prominent figures and cycling enthusiasts, united by a shared humanitarian goal of raising patients’ spirits and generating funds to improve the quality of medical care available to them. Overcoming challenges The ride was led by 68-year-old Guido De Wilde, who has recovered from stage four colon cancer and turned his personal experience into a commitment to helping others. Over the years, he has continued to support Al Jalila Foundation and raise funds for cancer patient care. Guido De Wilde said: “When we set off from Barcelona, we were determined to complete this journey for a cause close to our hearts: helping cancer patients access the care they need. Every kilometre brought us closer to our goal, and this experience has shown us what can be achieved when people come together for a shared purpose.” Strengthening a culture of giving The success of ‘Cycle Against Cancer’ reflects the UAE community’s culture of giving and charitable work, highlighting the importance of community initiatives in supporting healthcare and improving patients’ quality of life. The ride is among a series of initiatives supported annually by Al Jalila Foundation to encourage community participation and broaden charitable contributions towards healthcare.

headline: Centara Brings the Beauty and Charm of Thailand’s Loy Krathong Festival to the World
snippet: One Festival many Experiences – Centara Celebrates Loy Krathong Across Thailand, Japan and the Maldives Bangkok, Thailand – 12th November 2026 – Centara Hotels & Resorts, Thailand’s leading hotel operator, is a global ambassador that proudly brings the timeless elegance of Thai heritage to guests around the world. This November, as the “Land of Smiles” prepares to celebrate the annual festival of Loy Krathong, Centara invites travellers to discover what makes this one of Asia’s most enchanting cultural experiences. Every year under the soft glow of the full moon, Thai people gather at waterfronts across the kingdom to light candles and release “krathongs” – floating vessels crafted from woven leaves and illuminated with candles – into the water, to receive positive blessings for the year ahead. This November, couples, families and friends can mark Loy Krathong with a series of activities at Centara's hotels and resorts – not only in Thailand, but around the globe. From the Lanna-inspired banks of the Ping River and Hua Hin’s timeless seaside elegance to Bangkok’s contemporary celebrations, a playful coastal mood in Pattaya and new expressions of Thai culture overseas, Centara brings one cherished festival to life through many distinctive experiences. Classical and Contemporary Celebrations in Thailand Every Loy Krathong, Thailand’s rivers and lakes are transformed as hundreds of glowing krathongs float serenely on the rippling water. At Centara Riverside Hotel Chiang Mai, guests can feel blessed with the ancient spirit of the Lanna Kingdom with an authentic Northern Thai ritual overlooking the Ping River. Having savoured traditional cuisine and played temple fair games, loved ones can craft their own krathong then release it in the river, creating a moment of shared joy. One of Thailand’s most iconic and historic hotels, Centara Grand Beach Resort Hua Hin has captured the kingdom’s culture for more than 100 years. This Loy Krathong, Thai and international guests will be transported to the four culinary regions of Thailand with an exquisite dinner and barbecue, accompanied with classical Thai music and performances. Along the shores of Phuket’s Karon Beach, Centara Grand Beach Resort Phuket will bring Thai traditions to life with a charming beachfront celebration. Families can enjoy krathong-making workshops using natural materials, nostalgic temple fair-style games, and a festive buffet dinner at The Cove, complemented by traditional Thai cultural performances against the backdrop of the Andaman Sea. Meanwhile, Centara Grand Mirage Beach Resort Pattaya, the Lost World-themed family destination, underway for a playful celebration of Thai traditions under the concept “One Family, One Krathong, One Shared Moment.” From hands-on krathong-making and festive dining to interactive activities, the proposed programme is designed to bring families together and create lasting memories by the sea. In the pulsating heart of the Thai capital, Centara Grand at CentralWorld Bangkok raises its celebrations to the sky with a spectacular Loy Krathong - inspired pool party. This modern reimagining of a time-honoured festival will see revellers gather on the 26th floor pool deck, as the full moon shines over the city, for an upbeat evening of house music, drinks and dancing against Bangkok’s illuminated skyline. Centara Exports the Elegance of Loy Krathong to the World Centara will also bring the grace and beauty of Loy Krathong to guests at its international hotels and resorts this November, sharing authentic Thai-inspired hospitality in new settings. In Japan, Centara Grand Hotel Osaka will host a Lanna lantern-themed event at Suan Bua, its highly-acclaimed Thai restaurant. headline: Colorado pension fund commits $240m to hedge funds amid portfolio restructuring

headline: In Russia, global car brands are sold via parallel import, shifting warranty risk from factory to dealer
snippet: For buyers in Russia, the return of familiar global automotive brands to the market presents a paradox: while Toyota, Volkswagen, and Mazda are once again visible in showrooms, the emotional appeal of these logos has largely evaporated. The market is no longer defined by the prestige of European or Japanese engineering, but by a stark calculation of risk versus value. For the average consumer, the decision to purchase a "global" brand car is no longer a default choice but a complex logistical and financial challenge that often loses out to newer Chinese alternatives. The core misunderstanding driving this shift is the assumption that the appearance of these vehicles signals a restoration of official manufacturing and distribution networks. In reality, these cars are entering the Russian market through parallel import channels rather than direct factory partnerships. This distinction is critical. It means the traditional dealer structure, where a factory representative bears ultimate responsibility for quality control, warranty fulfillment, and service integrity, no longer exists. Instead, the buyer enters a transaction with an intermediary, shifting the burden of verifying the vehicle's legal provenance, technical condition, and long-term serviceability directly onto the individual owner. Statistical data confirms the scale of this structural shift. Over the first seven months of 2026, more than 100,000 new vehicles from global brands were registered in Russia. However, a significant portion of these arrivals were sourced from China. While the badge on the grille remains the same, the underlying product and its supply chain have fundamentally changed. This creates a disconnect between the consumer's expectation of a standardized global product and the reality of a vehicle whose specification may have been tailored exclusively for the Chinese domestic market.

headline: Rift Helium starts expanded 3D seismic acquisition in Tanzania
snippet: Aim-listed Rift Helium on November 10 started 3D seismic data acquisition at the Upepo project, in Tanzania’s Rukwa Basin, in line with previous guidance. The programme is designed to identify and rank potential helium traps ahead of exploration drilling planned for the first half of 2027, which the company highlights as an important step in its exploration strategy.
